about:
Abingdon Spares was founded in 1968 in Needham, Massachusetts, by Jerry Goguen, a sports-car enthusiast who also established the Westminster MG Car Museum in Vermont. The business began as a specialist supplier for MG T-series (TC, TD, TF) models.

The company stocks new-old-stock (NOS) and reproduction components for MG T-series and MGB vehicles, including engine internals, carburetion, fuel systems, braking, electrical, cooling, and body trim. Operating from a facility in Gorham, Maine, it maintains a comprehensive inventory of parts such as SU carburetor kits, wiring harnesses, brake components, and wood or sheet-metal body pieces. The catalog spans thousands of part numbers across mechanical, electrical, and cosmetic categories.

Abingdon Spares serves classic-car restorers, MG club members, and vintage-racing participants worldwide. Customers range from individual owners rebuilding a single TC to shops preparing MGBs for competition. The company also supplies technical resources—installation guides, identification charts, and a monthly “MG of the Month” feature—to support the enthusiast community.

The firm emphasizes depth of inventory and model-specific expertise, positioning itself as a single-source specialist for T-series and MGB parts. Its history of continuous operation under successive owners reflects a commitment to preserving the MG marque’s parts supply.
